A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GaitSnippet research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching content despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition experiments on six datasets across the main text and supplement, together with sampling, modeling, inference, and computational-cost analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments on four datasets and reports additional Gait3D frame-dropping and skeleton-map experiments in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The core sampling procedure, Snippet Blocks, pooling, and losses remain unchanged. Appendix A.3.6 adds skeleton-map inputs and a multimodal extension following SkeletonGait++ fusion, with both silhouette and skeleton branches replaced by snippet-based counterparts.

E1.justification: CASIA-B and OUMVLP evaluations are removed from the paper, including its appendix. CCPG and CCGR-MINI were already evaluated in v1 Table 10 and are retained, not newly added. New Gait3D scenarios cover missing frames, skeleton-map inputs, and combined silhouette/skeleton inputs, materially changing evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 11 adds evaluated comparisons with SkeletonGait and SkeletonGait++. Comparator sets for the retained Gait3D/GREW and CCPG/CCGR-MINI benchmark tables remain unchanged. GLN, SRN, and GQAN comparisons disappear with the removed laboratory-benchmark table.

E3.justification: v2 introduces test-time frame-retention ratios of 1, 1/2, 1/3, and 1/4 and separate skeleton-only and fused-input comparisons. It also explicitly reports rerunning CCPG with baseline-aligned preprocessing and protocols, although the precise differences from v1's preprocessing are unspecified. Core sampling settings and retained evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A.3.5–A.3.6 add direct tests of missing-frame robustness and transfer across input modalities, addressing important questions previously unsupported by corresponding experiments. Existing component, sampling, supervision, inference-partition, model-size, and backbone-transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Laboratory-benchmark results are removed, and the reported CCPG rerun replaces average rank-1 accuracy of 96.4% with 95.1% (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 2), without establishing a same-setting decline. New results include 66.2% versus 57.1% for DeepGaitV2-P3D with one-quarter frame retention, and 78.8% versus 77.6% for fused GaitSnippet versus SkeletonGait++. Original Gait3D/GREW headline results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The sampling assumptions and mathematical objectives are retained. Equations 1–2 expand the auxiliary distance expressions directly inside the losses without changing their mathematics; Equation 3 is unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: snippet-based gait representation, the sampling/modeling framework, and strong recognition using a 2D backbone. The headline 77.5% Gait3D and 81.7% GREW claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new experiments as supporting robustness through recurring gait cues and applicability beyond silhouettes, including multimodal modeling. It removes the discussion of laboratory-benchmark saturation and leading 3D methods. Existing limitations concerning partition ensembles and future temporal aggregation remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents CCPG/CCGR-MINI dataset statistics and describes the CCPG subject split; their previously described backbone settings are consolidated in Table 6. Laboratory-dataset implementation details and the explicit 64×44 preprocessing resolution are removed. Both PDFs still promise future code and pretrained-model release.

R1.justification: The CASIA-B reference by Yu et al. (2006) and OUMVLP reference by Takemura et al. (2018) are removed. Most related-work positioning remains intact. SkeletonGait was already cited in v1, but v2 additionally uses it and SkeletonGait++ to position the modality extensions.

P1.justification: Most explanatory prose remains closely matched. v2 makes localized wording revisions, introduces numbered method and ablation subsections, moves the CCPG/CCGR-MINI discussion and ethical statement into the main text, and adds reproducibility, acknowledgement, and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column ICLR layout, with figures and tables resized and relocated throughout. Figures 1–2 are redrawn into horizontal presentations. The laboratory comparison table is removed, v1 Table 10 becomes main-text Table 2, Tables 5–6 are revised, and new Tables 10–11 display the added analyses.

improvement.justification: The new missing-frame and modality-transfer experiments directly support robustness and applicability arguments that previously lacked corresponding tests. The explicitly reported baseline-aligned CCPG rerun also improves transparency. These provide a modest net improvement, tempered by removal of CASIA-B/OUMVLP evidence and the explicit preprocessing resolution. The central method and principal Gait3D/GREW results remain stable.
